name: Mem0
tagline: A persistent memory layer for agents, with Python and TypeScript SDKs and integrations.
hook: Maps each package to its own instructions and toolchain, then distinguishes the contribution gate for a change from the gate for an account.
summary: Mem0's packages use different languages, formatters, and tests, so the root guide starts with a routing table. A second table maps changes to required deliverables, followed by rules for accepted issues and contributor accounts.

techniques.title: Route by the edited package before running tools
techniques.body: The opening requires reading the nearest instructions and explains that line lengths, linters, and test runners differ. The routing table makes those differences visible before an agent applies a root-level default.
techniques.quote: Read the `AGENTS.md` nearest the files you are editing before running any command.

techniques.title: Explain a filename-sensitive workflow restriction
techniques.body: The Do NOT section requires maintainer approval for workflow changes. It ties that restriction to publishing credentials pinned to workflow filenames, giving the rule a concrete operational reason.
techniques.quote: - Modify anything in `.github/workflows/` without explicit maintainer approval. Publishing credentials are pinned to workflow filenames.

techniques.title: Map change types to supporting evidence
techniques.body: The shipping table distinguishes bug fixes, features, integrations, providers, and refactors. Bug fixes require a regression that fails without the change; public features also require docs and discovery updates.
techniques.quote: | **Bug fix** | A regression test that fails without the fix, written first. The fix. The relevant suite passing. The package's linter run. |

techniques.title: Separate change readiness from account recognition
techniques.body: The contribution section explains two independent gates. It states that being vouched does not bypass accepted-issue requirements, while absence from the list does not itself block a newcomer.
techniques.quote: Being vouched grants nothing. It is a "we have seen this person before" flag that mutes the newcomer comment, not permission to skip the accepted-issue rule. Being absent from the list costs nothing.

techniques.title: Describe recovery instead of encouraging gate bypasses
techniques.body: An unaccepted issue can close a PR automatically, and maintainer acceptance reopens it. The guide tells agents not to create duplicate submissions or manually work around that state machine.
techniques.quote: Do not work around either gate, do not reopen a gated pull request by hand, and do not re-file the same change under a new pull request when one is closed.

steal: Put package-specific tool differences in an instruction routing table.
Explain restrictions tied to publishing configuration.
Match verification and documentation to the type of change.
Separate account trust from acceptance of a proposed change.
Document how gated work can recover without duplicate submissions.
outline: What to ship with a change
